title: Pieces of diamond with the fewest dangling bonds
statement: Cut N atoms out of the diamond crystal: N distinct sites of the diamond lattice (integer points with all three coordinates even and x + y + z = 0 mod 4, or all three odd and x + y + z = 3 mod 4), connected through bonds, the pairs of sites at squared distance 3. In the crystal every atom has four bonds; the bonds to missing neighbours are dangling bonds, 4N - 2B of them when B bonds join the chosen atoms, and capping each with a hydrogen atom gives the hydrocarbon C_N H_(4N-2B) (adamantane, C10H16, for N = 10). Which N-atom pieces of diamond have the fewest dangling bonds, that is, the most bonds among N sites of the diamond lattice (its edge-isoperimetric problem)? The headline cell is N = 100: find a connected piece of 100 atoms with fewer than 72 dangling bonds (ours: C100H72, with 164 bonds).
submission: Text file: 100 lines 'x y z', distinct sites of the diamond lattice (all coordinates even with x + y + z = 0 mod 4, or all odd with x + y + z = 3 mod 4), connected through bonds (pairs at squared distance 3).
score: the number of dangling bonds 4N - 2B, the number of hydrogen atoms of the hydrocarbon (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: simulated annealing over 100-atom clusters started from the sites nearest a random centre, moving one atom at a time to an empty site next to the cluster, many restarts in 30 seconds (tools/src/diamond.c, mode anneal)

context: Diamond, silicon and germanium crystallise on the diamond lattice, each atom bonded to four neighbours at the corners of a tetrahedron. A finite piece of the crystal leaves dangling bonds on its surface; in hydrocarbons they are capped by hydrogen atoms, giving the diamondoids (adamantane C10H16, diamantane C14H20, triamantane C18H24 and the higher polymantanes found in petroleum) and hydrogen-terminated nanodiamonds, and in silicon they are the surface states of hydrogen-passivated nanocrystals. The oxygen atoms of cubic ice Ic sit on the same lattice, so the most hydrogen-bonded clusters of N water molecules cut from cubic ice are the same pieces. Counting dangling bonds turns the question into the edge-isoperimetric problem of the diamond lattice: which N vertices of this 4-regular graph span the most edges? The problem is solved exactly for the square, triangular and hexagonal lattices (Harary and Harborth 1976) and for the integer grid Z^d (Bollobas and Leader 1991; Ahlswede and Bezrukov 1995), and asymptotically for Cayley graphs on Z^d (Barber and Erde 2018), but the diamond lattice, which is not a lattice in the group sense (its two sublattices point their bonds in opposite directions), is not covered. Chemists have enumerated the diamondoids built from whole adamantane cages (Balaban and Schleyer 1978) and computed the stabilities of those with up to 41 carbon atoms, but the fewest dangling bonds over all pieces of the crystal, cages or not, has not been asked as far as our searches show. The exact values below come from an exhaustive enumeration of every connected cluster with up to 17 atoms (our counts of clusters agree with OEIS A039740); beyond that our values come from annealing.
references: F. Harary, H. Harborth, Extremal animals, J. Combin. Inform. System Sci. 1 (1976) 1-8
B. Bollobas, I. Leader, Edge-isoperimetric inequalities in the grid, Combinatorica 11 (1991) 299-314
R. Ahlswede, S. L. Bezrukov, Edge isoperimetric theorems for integer point arrays, Appl. Math. Lett. 8 (1995) 75-80
B. Barber, J. Erde, Isoperimetry in integer lattices, Discrete Analysis 2018:7
A. T. Balaban, P. von R. Schleyer, Systematic classification and nomenclature of diamond hydrocarbons I: graph-theoretical enumeration of polymantanes, Tetrahedron 34 (1978) 3599-3609
OEIS A039740: lattice animals in the cubic diamond lattice (the cluster counts of our enumeration)

novelty.verdict: new question for the diamond lattice: the edge-isoperimetric problem (most bonds among N sites) is solved or studied for Z^d and the planar lattices, and diamondoids made of whole adamantane cages are enumerated, but no one has asked for the fewest dangling bonds over all N-atom pieces of the diamond lattice, as far as our searches show.
closest: Edge-isoperimetric problems on lattices (Harary and Harborth 1976 for the planar lattices; Bollobas and Leader 1991 and Ahlswede and Bezrukov 1995 for Z^d; Barber and Erde 2018 asymptotically for Cayley graphs on Z^d; Strachan and Swanepoel, arXiv:2503.09591): the same question on other lattices; the diamond lattice is not among them.

Diamondoid enumerations (Balaban and Schleyer 1978; a 2018 study of the diamondoids CnHm with 10 to 41 carbons): only pieces made of whole adamantane cages, ranked by stability, not the extremal count over all pieces.
Hydrogen-passivated silicon nanocrystals and nanodiamond shapes (closed-form CH counts for truncated tetrahedra, arXiv:2111.04490): particular shapes, not the minimum for each N.
novelty.benchmark: no cluster or isoperimetric family in the benchmark

first_values.note: Exact values: every connected cluster of the diamond lattice with N <= 17 atoms, enumerated by Redelmeier's method from an A and from a B origin (tools/src/diamond.c, mode exact; the counts are those of OEIS A039740, with the one-atom cluster counted once from each origin). Best known values: tools/src/diamond.c, mode anneal, 30 s and two seeds for each N (both seeds agree). The checker counts bonds and checks connectivity exactly.

baseline.text: 72 dangling bonds (C100H72: 100 atoms, 164 bonds), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the cluster in `refs/diamond-bonds.txt`.

cells.title: Piece of diamond with {N} atoms and the fewest dangling bonds
cells.statement: Choose {N} distinct sites of the diamond lattice (integer points with all three coordinates even and x + y + z = 0 mod 4, or all three odd and x + y + z = 3 mod 4), connected through bonds (pairs at squared distance 3), with the most bonds B among them, that is the fewest dangling bonds 4 x {N} - 2B (the hydrogen atoms of the hydrocarbon C_{N}H_(4 x {N} - 2B)).
cells.submission: Text file: {N} lines 'x y z', distinct connected sites of the diamond lattice.
cells.exact_how: the value of the enumeration of every connected cluster with at most 17 sites (Redelmeier's method, tools/src/diamond.c, mode exact); the certificate is a cluster of that value
cells.how: simulated annealing over connected clusters (tools/src/diamond.c, mode anneal)
